# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — HAFNIA LIMITED (HAFN)

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW
| Item | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | HAFN / Hafnia Limited (NYSE; OSE: HAFNI) | [Actual] |

| Bull IV | **$15.95** (+55.2%) | [Estimate] |

Hafnia is a product-tanker owner (~180 vessels, part of the 80-year BW Group) at a 52-week high after a +48% six-month run. My cycle-adjusted DCF lands essentially at market price: the market is roughly correctly pricing (a) the current Hormuz/Red Sea freight spike and (b) the ~20% TORM consolidation option, against a forward curve that is already rolling over. Standalone value says **HOLD**; the strong, fundamentally-backed uptrend supports a small **momentum Accumulate** that is sold when the trend breaks.

## SECTION 1 — MACRO
- **Rates / regime:** rf (nominal 10y) 5.24%, real 2.88%, breakeven 2.36% [Actual, DATA 1.5]. Regime vector is contested — goldilocks 0.341 headline but margin only 0.070; tightening 0.176, stagflation 0.130 [Actual]. A high-rate, sticky-inflation regime (CPI 3.35%, PCE 3.42%) keeps the discount rate elevated and caps multiples on a commodity cyclical.
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock` (severity 1, direction up, onset 2026-09-28) [Actual, DATA 1.6]. The Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed again (re-closed early July 2026 per PRIMARY P1); Gulf exports fell 2.1 mb/d to 15 mb/d in July; SUMED saw Saudi exports surge to 1.25 mb/d (highest since Apr 2020) [Actual, PRIMARY P1].
- **Exposure:** Hafnia's earnings are a direct function of product-tanker TCEs, which are being pushed up by war-risk fragmentation and longer voyage distances (tonne-miles). The IEA now forecasts global oil demand contracting 1.6 mb/d in 2026 to 103.3 mb/d [Actual, PRIMARY P1] — so the rate premium is being driven by *supply/routing* disruption, not demand growth. That makes the premium fragile: it reverses with a durable Hormuz reopening and the return of Gulf/Asian refining capacity. This is the single most important macro input and the core Bear transmission path.
- **Cost-of-capital anchor:** COE ANCHOR 9.04% = rf_eff 5.24% + 0.912× loading × 4.17% market-consistent premium [Actual, DATA 1.5]. I use it unchanged (no >150bp departure).

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT
**Economic engines (Mandate 1):**
1. **Transactional deliveries (dominant, ~95%+ of earnings):** Product-tanker TCE income from a fleet of LR2/LR1/MR/Handy vessels. Purely cyclical — Q2 2026 TCE income $372.9M at $44,093/day vs $231.2M in Q2 2025 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. No pricing power; rates are spot/period-set.
2. **Captive installed-base annuity (small but real):** Fee-based businesses (technical management, disponent-owner pool management, bunker procurement desk) generated $8.8M in Q2 2026 and $16.6M in H1 2026 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. This is a recurring stream on the ~180-vessel installed base, but it is <5% of earnings — it cushions, it does not drive.
3. **Strategic optionality (the new engine):** The ~19.85% TORM stake (~$0.705B ≈ $1.32/share at TORM's ~$3.55B market cap) [Estimate; stake % Actual per PRIMARY P6, TORM mkt cap from Yahoo 9/23/2026] plus the new asset-management CEO's "case for scale." This is merger/control optionality on a major product-tanker rival — it adds consolidation upside (Bull) but also deepens correlation to the same rate cycle (Bear).

**Owner earnings after SBC (Mandate 2):** SBC is immaterial ($0.002–0.003B/yr, DATA 5) and is already expensed in net income; I treat it as **deducted_in_cf** (counted once, no double deduction). Base owner earnings = $0.926B (DEFAULTS, FY2024-based: NI $0.774B + D&A $0.215B − capex $0.050B) [Actual inputs, Estimate base]. Note the FY2024 capex figure ($50M, PPE only) is 2.95× below the vendor's $146M (which includes capitalized software/newbuilds); I keep the filed figure but flag the FCF-overstatement risk in SECTION 10.

**Moat rating (7 factors, 0–3 each; total /21 → 1.0–5.0):**
| Factor | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Pricing power | 1 | Spot/period-set rates; current highs are a geopolitical shock, not durable power |
| Switching costs / lock-in | 1 | Vessels fungible; low charterer switching; some pool/fee stickiness |
| Scale / cost advantage | 2 | ~180 vessels, "lowest cost operator," bunker & technical scale |
| Fleet quality / asset edge | 2 | Young, efficient, IMO II-compliant; advantaged as sanctions tighten supply |
| Brand / network | 2 | Strong global brand, 80-yr BW Group, 4 hubs |
| Entry barriers / regulatory | 2 | $40–50M/vessel capital, IMO compliance, sanctioned-fleet expansion |
| Installed base / recurring rev | 2 | Fee-based annuity ($16.6M H1 2026) on the installed base |
| **Total** | **12/21 → 3.3/5.0** | Moderate moat; direction stable-to-slightly-eroding (core freight purely cyclical) |

**Financial strength:** Net LTV fell from 20.2% (Q1) to 13.0% (Q2 2026); equity ratio 66.9%; the $300M placement (Sept 2026) left net LTV ~13% [Actual, PRIMARY P1/P3]. Strong balance sheet — it funds the 90% payout, the TORM build, and cushions the Bear case.

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION
**Frame & shares:** Equity frame (all flows are after-interest). Shares = 535,331,154 (DEFAULTS, post-placement count per PRIMARY P3) [Actual]. Excess cash = $0.284B (DEFAULTS base-year cash; the desk refuses higher — see SECTION 10 on the stale-cash caveat).

My implied terminal multiple (15.3×) sits right at the cluster median. The stock trades at T0/next-FY EPS $0.71 ≈ **14.5×** normalized earnings — in line with the peer median. Consistent with "fairly valued," not rich or cheap on a normalized basis.

**Neutral reverse DCF (Mandate 3b):** Under the neutral structure (9.0% CoE, 3.8% terminal-g, 10-yr fade), today's price implies a **10-year CAGR of −10.6%** (solved initial growth −27.1%). That sits **below the p50 (5.6%)** of the $1–10B base-rate bucket — i.e., the market is *not* pricing in sustained above-median growth; it is pricing in a cyclical roll-down, which is exactly what my Base models.
